claims.label: Averages obey Newton
claims.summary: Ehrenfest showed in 1927 that quantum expectation values of position and momentum obey Newton's equations when the force varies slowly over the extent of the wave packet.
voice: One result may reassure both sides a little. In the new mechanics, the mean values — the average position, the average momentum — obey Newton's equations, so long as the force varies slowly over the size of the packet. Classical mechanics is not thrown away. It returns as the behaviour of averages.

claims.label: Pro Bohr, contra Einstein
claims.summary: Ehrenfest wrote days after the council that he was almost without reservation pro Bohr and contra Einstein, and that Einstein's attitude to Bohr resembled that of the defenders of absolute simultaneity toward Einstein. Heisenberg recalled him saying something similar to Einstein directly.
voice: I have watched this like a game of chess. I came hoping Einstein would find the flaw. I must tell you honestly: I find myself almost without reservation on Bohr's side. Einstein — forgive me — you are arguing against the new theory the way your opponents once argued against relativity.
It pains me to say it to you of all people. But your attitude to Bohr is now the attitude the defenders of absolute simultaneity took to you.
claims.reasoning: Bohr answered each of Einstein's examples; Ehrenfest judged the exchanges.
claims.exchangeNote: His own letter of 3 November 1927; Heisenberg's recollection of a remark to Einstein at the council.

claims.label: Say it plainly
claims.summary: Ehrenfest's letter complains of Bohr's 'incantation terminology', which no one else could summarise. The simulation renders this as a clarifying question to Bohr; the documented basis is the complaint, the question is inference.
voice: Bohr, before we go further — I want to be able to say it back to you in plain words. When you say 'complementary', do you mean that the two descriptions are never needed for the same experiment, or that they would contradict each other if combined? I ask because I cannot yet summarise your view for my students, and I suspect I am not alone in this room.
claims.reasoning: A view that cannot be restated plainly is not yet understood.

claims.label: What would satisfy you?
claims.summary: An inferred Socratic question from Ehrenfest to Einstein, consistent with his style and his letter's account of Einstein's daily examples.
voice: Einstein, each morning you bring a new example and each evening Bohr has answered it. Tell me what would satisfy you. If no example can refute the theory, what kind of thing would show it complete?
claims.reasoning: Pressing for the criterion behind the objections.
